# STOCK PURCHASE AGREEMENT

This STOCK PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this "**Agreement**" or the "**Purchase Agreement**") is entered into as of August 14, 2026, by and among **Daikesk Imaging Holdings, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Buyer**"), **Glosiv Medical Systems, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Seller**"), and **Sorrelux Imaging, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation (the "**Company**").

## RECITALS

A. Seller owns all of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock, par value $0.001 per share, of the Company (the "**Shares**").

B. The Company is engaged in the Business.

C. Seller wishes to sell to Buyer, and Buyer wishes to purchase from Seller, all of the Shares on the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

## ARTICLE I. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 Definitions.** The following terms have the meanings set forth below:

"**Affiliate**" means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by or is under common control with that Person.

"**Ancillary Agreements**" means the Transition Services Agreement and the Key Employee Agreement.

"**Business**" means the design, manufacture, sale and servicing of digital radiography and ultrasound imaging systems.

"**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or day on which banks in New York, New York or Wilmington, Delaware are authorized or required by law to close.

"**Closing**" and "**Closing Date**" have the meanings given in Section 3.1.

"**Company Data**" means all data, records and information owned by, licensed to or held for the Company, including customer lists, installed-base records, field-service histories, device performance data and protected health information processed by or for the Company.

"**Company Intellectual Property**" means all Intellectual Property owned by, or licensed to, the Company and used or held for use in the Business.

"**Confidential Information**" has the meaning given in Section 6.7.

"**Disclosure Schedule**" means the disclosure schedule delivered by Seller to Buyer on the date of this Agreement.

"**Fraud**" means actual and intentional fraud under Delaware law in the making of the representations and warranties in this Agreement.

"**Fundamental Representations**" means the representations and warranties in Section 4.1 (Organization and Good Standing), Section 4.2 (Authority), Section 4.3 (Capitalization; Title to Shares) and Section 4.14 (Brokers).

"**Governmental Authority**" means any federal, state, local or foreign government or any agency, court or regulatory body, including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

"**Intellectual Property**" means patents, patent applications, trademarks, copyrights, software, trade secrets, know-how and all other intellectual property rights.

"**Key Employee**" means Dr. Tamsin Ferreol, Chief Technology Officer of the Company.

"**Key Employee Agreement**" means the Employment Agreement between the Company and the Key Employee dated March 15, 2021.

"**Losses**" means losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees.

"**Material Adverse Effect**" means any event, change or effect that is, or would reasonably be expected to be, materially adverse to the business, assets, financial condition or results of operations of the Company, taken as a whole, other than effects arising from general economic conditions, changes in law or GAAP, or the announcement of this Agreement, except to the extent such effects disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the medical imaging industry.

"**Material Contracts**" has the meaning given in Section 4.8.

"**Person**" means any individual, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, trust, Governmental Authority or other entity.

"**Transition Services Agreement**" means the Transition Services Agreement between Seller, as provider, and the Company, as recipient, in the form attached as Exhibit A.

**1.2 Interpretation.** Headings are for convenience only. "Including" means "including without limitation." References to Articles, Sections, Schedules and Exhibits are to those of this Agreement unless otherwise stated.

## ARTICLE II. PURCHASE AND SALE

**2.1 Purchase and Sale; Purchase Price.** At the Closing, Seller shall sell, assign and transfer to Buyer, and Buyer shall purchase from Seller, all of the Shares, free and clear of all liens, for an aggregate purchase price of $186,500,000 (the "**Purchase Price**"), subject to adjustment under Section 2.3.

**2.2 Payment at Closing.** At the Closing, Buyer shall pay by wire transfer of immediately available funds:

(a) $9,325,000 (the "**Escrow Amount**") to Wilmington Escrow Services, LLC, as escrow agent, to be held under an escrow agreement in customary form as a source of recovery for claims under Article IX; and

(b) the Purchase Price, as adjusted by the Estimated Working Capital Adjustment, less the Escrow Amount, to an account designated by Seller in writing at least three Business Days before the Closing Date.

**2.3 Working Capital Adjustment.**

(a) At least three Business Days before the Closing, Seller shall deliver to Buyer a good-faith estimate of the Company's Closing Working Capital. The Purchase Price paid at Closing shall be increased or decreased, as applicable, by the amount by which estimated Closing Working Capital exceeds or falls short of $14,200,000 (the "**Target Working Capital**") (the "**Estimated Working Capital Adjustment**").

(b) Within 90 days after the Closing Date, Buyer shall deliver to Seller a statement of the Company's actual Closing Working Capital. Seller has 30 days to object in writing. Disputes not resolved within 30 days after an objection shall be submitted to an independ

ent accounting firm mutually agreed by the parties, whose determination is final and binding absent manifest error.

(c) Any amount owed following the final determination shall be paid within five Business Days by wire transfer.

"**Closing Working Capital**" means current assets of the Company (excluding cash and tax assets) less current liabilities of the Company (excluding indebtedness and tax liabilities), determined in accordance with GAAP consistently applied.

**2.4 Withholding.** Buyer may deduct and withhold from any amount payable under this Agreement any amount required to be withheld under applicable tax law.

## ARTICLE III. CLOSING

**3.1 Closing.** The closing of the purchase and sale of the Shares (the "**Closing**") shall take place remotely by electronic exchange of documents on the third Business Day after satisfaction or waiver of the conditions in Article VII (other than conditions to be satisfied at the Closing), or on another date agreed by Buyer and Seller (the "**Closing Date**").

**3.2 Seller Closing Deliverables.** At the Closing, Seller shall deliver to Buyer:

(a) stock certificates representing the Shares, duly endorsed in blank, or stock powers duly executed;

(b) the Transition Services Agreement, duly executed by Seller and the Company;

(c) written resignations of the directors and officers of the Company designated by Buyer;

(d) the certificate described in Section 7.2(c);

(e) a properly completed IRS Form W-9 of Seller; and

(f) the third-party consents listed on Schedule 4.5.

**3.3 Buyer Closing Deliverables.** At the Closing, Buyer shall deliver the payments described in Section 2.2 and the certificate described in Section 7.3(c).

## ARTICLE IV. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF SELLER

Except as set forth in the Disclosure Schedule, Seller represents and warrants to Buyer as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as follows:

**4.1 Organization and Good Standing.** Each of Seller and the Company is a corporation duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware and has all requisite corporate power to own its assets and conduct its business as now conducted.

**4.2 Authority.** Seller has full corporate power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements to which it is a party. This Agreement has been duly authorized, executed and delivered by Seller and constitutes its legal, valid and binding obligation, enforceable in accordance with its terms.

**4.3 Capitalization; Title to Shares.** The authorized capital stock of the Company consists of 10,000,000 shares of common stock, of which 1,000,000 shares are issued and outstanding, all of which are the Shares. Seller is the record and beneficial owner of the Shares, free and clear of all liens. There are no options, warrants or other rights to acquire any equity of the Company.

**4.4 No Conflicts.** The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by Seller do not (a) violate the certificate of incorporation or bylaws of Seller or the Company, (b) violate any law applicable to Seller or the Company, or (c) except as set forth on Schedule 4.5, result in a breach of, or give rise to any right of termination under, any Material Contract.

**4.5 Consents.** No consent, approval, waiver or authorization of, or notice to, any Governmental Authority or other Person is required in connection with the execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by Seller or the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, except those set forth on Schedule 4.5.

**4.6 Financial Statements.** Seller has delivered to Buyer the audited balance sheets of the Company as of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2025, and the related statements of income and cash flows for the years then ended, and the unaudited balance sheet of the Company as of June 30, 2026 and related statements for the six months then ended. The financial statements were prepared in accordance with GAAP consistently applied and fairly present in all material respects the financial position of the Company as of their dates.

**4.7 Absence of Changes.** Since December 31, 2025, the Company has conducted the Business in the ordinary course and there has not been any Material Adverse Effect.

**4.8 Material Contracts.** Schedule 4.8 lists each contract to which the Company is a party that (a) involves annual payments in excess of $500,000, (b) is a license of Intellectual Property to or from the Company (other than off-the-shelf software), (c) is an employment agreement with any officer of the Company, (d) is a group purchasing, distribution or supply arrangement with a hospital system or group purchasing organization, or (e) restricts the Company from competing in any line of business (the "**Material Contracts**"). Each Material Contract is valid and in full force and effect, and neither the Company nor, to Seller's knowledge, any counterparty is in material breach.

**4.9 Intellectual Property.** The Company owns, or has a valid and enforceable right to use, all Company Intellectual Property necessary for the conduct of the Business as currently conducted. To Seller's knowledge, the conduct of the Business does not infringe the Intellectual Property of any Person.

**4.10 Regulatory Compliance.** The Company holds all FDA 510(k) clearances and other permits required for the products of the Business, and is in compliance in all material respects with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and applicable quality system regulations.

**4.11 Data Privacy.** The Company is in compliance in all material respects with HIPAA and all other applicable laws relating to the privacy and security of Company Data. Since January 1, 2023, there has been no material breach of security involving Company Data.

**4.12 Employees.** Schedule 4.12 lists each employee of the Company with annual base compensation in excess of $200,000. The

 Company is not party to any collective bargaining agreement.

**4.13 Taxes.** The Company has timely filed all material tax returns required to be filed and has paid all taxes shown as due on those returns.

**4.14 Brokers.** No broker, finder or investment banker is entitled to any fee or commission from the Company or Seller in connection with this Agreement, other than Halvern Partners LLC, whose fees will be paid by Seller.

## ARTICLE V. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF BUYER

Buyer represents and warrants to Seller as follows:

**5.1 Organization; Authority.** Buyer is a corporation duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware and has full corporate power to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.

**5.2 No Conflicts; Consents.** The execution and performance of this Agreement by Buyer do not violate Buyer's organizational documents or any law applicable to Buyer, and require no consent of any Governmental Authority other than under the HSR Act.

**5.3 Sufficiency of Funds.** Buyer will have at the Closing sufficient immediately available funds to pay the Purchase Price.

**5.4 Investment Intent.** Buyer is acquiring the Shares for its own account and not with a view to distribution in violation of securities laws.

## ARTICLE VI. COVENANTS

**6.1 Conduct of Business.** From the date of this Agreement until the Closing, except as consented to in writing by Buyer, Seller shall cause the Company to operate the Business in the ordinary course consistent with past practice and to preserve its relationships with customers, suppliers and employees. Without limiting the foregoing, the Company shall not amend, terminate or waive any material right under any Material Contract.

**6.2 Access.** Until the Closing, Seller shall give Buyer and its representatives reasonable access during normal business hours to the properties, books, records and personnel of the Company.

**6.3 Efforts; Regulatory Filings.** Each party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to satisfy the conditions in Article VII. Each party shall file any notification required under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976 (the "**HSR Act**") within ten Business Days after the date of this Agreement.

**6.4 Third-Party Consents.** Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, before the Closing, each consent listed on Schedule 4.5.

**6.5 Exclusivity.** Until the earlier of the Closing and the termination of this Agreement, Seller shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, solicit, negotiate or enter into any agreement with respect to the sale of the Company or its material assets with any Person other than Buyer.

**6.6 Notification.** Seller shall promptly notify Buyer of any fact or event that would reasonably be expected to cause any condition in Section 7.2 not to be satisfied.

**6.7 Confidentiality.** From and after the Closing, Seller shall, and shall cause its Affiliates and their respective representatives to, hold in confidence and not use or disclose any confidential or proprietary information concerning the Company or the Business, including Company Data and Company Intellectual Property ("**Confidential Information**"), except (a) to the extent the information becomes publicly available other than through breach of this Section 6.7, (b) as required by law, after prompt notice to Buyer, or (c) as necessary to perform the Transition Services Agreement.

**6.8 Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation.** For five years after the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly (a) engage in the Business anywhere in North America or Europe, (b) own any interest in any Person engaged in the Business (other than passive holdings of less than 2% of a publicly traded company), or (c) solicit for employment any employee of the Company with annual base compensation in excess of $150,000, except through general solicitations not targeted at Company employees.

**6.9 Public Announcements.** No party shall issue any press release regarding this Agreement without the prior consent of Buyer and Seller, except as required by law.

**6.10 Intercompany Arrangements.** At or before the Closing, Seller shall cause all intercompany accounts and agreements between the Company and Seller or its Affiliates to be settled and terminated, other than the Transition Services Agreement.

## ARTICLE VII. CONDITIONS TO CLOSING

**7.1 Conditions to Obligations of All Parties.** The obligations of each party to consummate the Closing are subject to satisfaction of the following conditions:

(a) any waiting period under the HSR Act shall have expired or been terminated; and

(b) no Governmental Authority shall have enacted or issued any law or order that prohibits the Closing.

**7.2 Conditions to Obligations of Buyer.** The obligation of Buyer to consummate the Closing is subject to satisfaction, or waiver by Buyer, of the following conditions:

(a) the Fundamental Representations shall be true and correct in all respects, and the other representations and warranties of Seller shall be true and correct in all material respects, in each case as of the Closing Date;

(b) Seller shall have performed in all material respects all covenants required to be performed by it before the Closing;

(c) Buyer shall have received a certificate of an officer of Seller certifying the satisfaction of the conditions in Sections 7.2(a), (b) and (d);

(d) no Material Adverse Effect shall have occurred since the date of this Agreement;

(e) the consents listed on Schedule 4.5 shall have been obtained; and

(f) Seller shall have delivered the items listed in Section 3.2.

**7.3 Conditions to Obligations of Seller.** The obligation of Seller to consummate the Closing is subject to satisfaction, or waiver by Seller, of the following conditions:

(a) the representations and warranties of Buyer shall be true and correct in all material respect

s as of the Closing Date;

(b) Buyer shall have performed in all material respects all covenants required to be performed by it before the Closing; and

(c) Seller shall have received a certificate of an officer of Buyer to that effect.

## ARTICLE VIII. TERMINATION

**8.1 Termination.** This Agreement may be terminated before the Closing:

(a) by mutual written consent of Buyer and Seller;

(b) by Buyer or Seller if the Closing has not occurred by December 31, 2026, provided that the terminating party's breach is not the principal cause of the delay;

(c) by Buyer if Seller has breached any representation or covenant such that a condition in Section 7.2 would not be satisfied, and the breach is not cured within 30 days after notice; or

(d) by Seller if Buyer has breached any representation or covenant such that a condition in Section 7.3 would not be satisfied, and the breach is not cured within 30 days after notice.

**8.2 Effect of Termination.** On termination, this Agreement shall be void and of no further effect, except that this Section 8.2 and Article XI shall survive, and no party shall be relieved of liability for willful breach before termination.

## ARTICLE IX. INDEMNIFICATION

**9.1 Survival.** The representations and warranties in this Agreement survive the Closing for 18 months, except that the Fundamental Representations survive until 60 days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Covenants survive until fully performed.

**9.2 Indemnification by Seller.** From and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer, the Company and their Affiliates against all Losses arising out of (a) any breach of any representation or warranty of Seller, (b) any breach of any covenant of Seller, or (c) any taxes of the Company for pre-Closing periods.

**9.3 Indemnification by Buyer.** From and after the Closing, Buyer shall indemnify Seller and its Affiliates against all Losses arising out of any breach of any representation, warranty or covenant of Buyer.

**9.4 Limitations.**

(a) Seller's aggregate liability under Section 9.2(a) shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price ($18,650,000). Seller shall not be liable under Section 9.2(a) until aggregate Losses exceed $1,400,000, after which Seller shall be liable for all Losses from the first dollar.

(b) The limitations in Section 9.4(a) do not apply to Losses arising out of Fraud, any breach of the Fundamental Representations, or any breach of Section 6.7 (Confidentiality). Seller's aggregate liability for those Losses shall not exceed the Purchase Price, except in the case of Fraud.

(c) Buyer's aggregate liability under Section 9.3 shall not exceed the amount set forth in Section 9.4(a), except for breaches of Section 5.1 and Fraud.

**9.5 Procedures.** An indemnified party shall give prompt written notice of any claim, describing it in reasonable detail. For third-party claims, the indemnifying party may assume the defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified party, and shall not settle any claim without the indemnified party's consent unless the settlement involves only the payment of money and a full release.

**9.6 Escrow; Order of Recovery.** Buyer shall first seek recovery of Losses under Section 9.2(a) from the Escrow Amount, and then directly from Seller.

**9.7 Exclusive Remedy.** Except for claims for Fraud and claims for specific performance or injunctive relief under Section 11.10, this Article IX is the exclusive remedy of the parties after the Closing for any breach of this Agreement.

## ARTICLE X. TAX MATTERS

**10.1 Tax Returns.** Seller shall prepare all tax returns of the Company for periods ending on or before the Closing Date. Buyer shall prepare all other tax returns of the Company.

**10.2 Straddle Periods.** Taxes for any period beginning before and ending after the Closing Date shall be apportioned on a closing-of-the-books basis, except for property taxes, which shall be apportioned daily.

**10.3 Transfer Taxes.** Transfer, stamp and similar taxes arising from the sale of the Shares shall be borne equally by Buyer and Seller.

**10.4 Cooperation.** Buyer and Seller shall cooperate reasonably in the filing of tax returns and in any audit relating to taxes of the Company.

## ARTICLE XI. MISCELLANEOUS

**11.1 Expenses.** Except as otherwise provided, each party bears its own expenses in connection with this Agreement.

**11.2 Notices.** Notices must be in writing and are effective on delivery by hand, nationally recognized overnight courier or email (with confirmation of transmission), addressed:

If to Buyer: Daikesk Imaging Holdings, Inc., Attention: General Counsel.

If to Seller: Glosiv Medical Systems, Inc., Attention: Chief Legal Officer.

If to the Company before the Closing, to Seller; after the Closing, to Buyer.

**11.3 Amendment; Waiver.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by Buyer and Seller. No waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving party.

**11.4 Assignment.** No party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other parties, except that Buyer may assign its rights to any Affiliate or, after the Closing, to any acquirer of all or substantially all of the Company's assets, provided Buyer remains liable for its obligations.

**11.5 Successors.** This Agreement binds and benefits the parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

**11.6 No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** Except for the indemnified parties under Article IX, nothing in this Agreement confers any right on any Person other than the parties.

**11.7 Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, the remaining provisions remain in full force, and the invalid provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to be enforceable.

**11.8 Governing Law.** This Agreement and all claims arising out of or relating to it are governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict

-of-laws principles that would require the application of the laws of another jurisdiction.

**11.9 Exclusive Forum; Waiver of Jury Trial.** Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if that court lacks subject-matter jurisdiction, the Superior Court of the State of Delaware or the United States District Court for the District of Delaware) for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement. EACH PARTY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY SUCH ACTION.

**11.10 Specific Performance.** The parties agree that irreparable damage would occur if any provision of this Agreement were not performed in accordance with its terms, and that each party is entitled to specific performance and injunctive relief, without posting bond, in addition to any other remedy.

**11.11 Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which constitute one instrument.

**11.12 Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict among this Agreement and the Ancillary Agreements, the following order of precedence applies: the Purchase Agreement, then the Transition Services Agreement, then the Key Employee Agreement; each Ancillary Agreement controls as to its own subject matter.

# EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

This EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of March 15, 2021 (the "**Effective Date**"), by and between **Sorrelux Imaging, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation (the "**Company**"), and **Dr. Tamsin Ferreol**, an individual (the "**Employee**").

## RECITALS

A. The Company designs, manufactures, sells and services digital radiography and ultrasound imaging systems.

B. The Employee is the sole owner and named inventor of certain patents relating to the calibration of flat-panel digital radiography detectors. She conceived and reduced those inventions to practice before the Effective Date and outside any employment with the Company.

C. The Company wishes to employ the Employee as its Chief Technology Officer and to obtain a license to those patents. The Employee wishes to accept that employment and grant that license on the terms of this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises in this Agreement, the parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 Defined Terms.** The following terms have the meanings set forth below:

"**Base Salary**" has the meaning given in Section 4.1.

"**Board**" means the Board of Directors of the Company.

"**Cause**" means the Employee's (a) conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony; (b) willful misconduct or gross negligence in the performance of her duties that causes material harm to the Company; (c) material breach of Section 8 or Section 10; or (d) willful and continued failure to perform her material duties, after written notice from the Board and a cure period of 30 days.

"**Change of Control**" means any of the following: (a) any Person or group of Persons acting together acquires, directly or indirectly, beneficial ownership of more than 50% of the outstanding voting stock of the Company, whether by purchase, merger or otherwise, including any sale of a majority of the Company's stock; (b) a merger or consolidation of the Company in which the holders of the Company's voting stock immediately before the transaction hold less than 50% of the voting power of the surviving entity immediately after it; or (c) a sale, lease or other disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of the Company.

"**Company Products**" means the digital radiography and ultrasound imaging systems, detectors, components, software and related service offerings that the Company designs, manufactures, sells or services from time to time.

"**Confidential Information**" has the meaning given in Section 8.1.

"**Detector Calibration Patents**" means the patents and patent applications listed on Exhibit A, together with all continuations, continuations-in-part, divisionals, reissues, reexaminations and extensions of them, and all foreign counterparts.

"**Good Reason**" means, without the Employee's written consent, (a) a material reduction in the Base Salary; (b) a material diminution in her title, authority or duties; or (c) relocation of her principal place of work by more than 50 miles. Good Reason exists only if the Employee gives written notice within 60 days after the condition first arises, the Company fails to cure within 30 days after that notice, and the Employee resigns within 30 days after the cure period ends.

"**Inventions**" has the meaning given in Section 9.1.

"**Person**" means any individual, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, trust, governmental authority or other entity.

**1.2 Interpretation.** Headings are for convenience only. "Including" means "including without limitation."

## 2. EMPLOYMENT AND DUTIES

**2.1 Position.** The Company employs the Employee as its Chief Technology Officer. She reports to the Chief Executive Officer of the Company.

**2.2 Duties.** The Employee shall have the duties, authority and responsibilities customary for a chief technology officer of a medical imaging company. These include leadership of research and development, detector and transducer engineering, product software and regulatory design controls, together with any other duties the Chief Executive Officer reasonably assigns.

**2.3 Full Time and Attention.** The Employee shall devote substantially all of her business time and attention to the Company. She may serve on scientific advisory boards, hold academic appointments, and manage her personal investments, provided those activities do not materially interfere with her duties or breach Section 8 or Section 10.

**2.4 Place of Performance.** The Employee's principal place of work is the Company's headquarters, subject to reasonable business travel.

## 3. TERM

**3.1 Initial Term.** The term of employment begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years (the "**Initial Term**").

**3.2 Renewal.** At the end of the Initial Term and each anniversary after it, the term renews automatically for successive one-year periods. Either party may prevent a renewal by giving written notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before the renewal date. The Initial Term and any renewals are the "**Term**."

## 4. COMPENSATION

**4.1 Base Salary.** The Company shall pay the Employee an annual base salary of $345,000 (the "**Base Salary**"), payable in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices. The Board shall review the Base Salary at least annually and may increase it, but not decrease it.

**4.2 Annual Bonus.** The Employee is eligible for an annual cash bonus with a target of 40% of Base Salary. The bonus is based on Company and individual performance objectives that the Board sets after consultation with the Employee. Any bonus is paid no later than March 15 of the year following the year to which it relates.

**4.3 Long-Term Incentive.** The Employee is eligible to participate in any long-term incentive plan that the Company or its parent maintains for senior executives. Her participation is on terms no less favorable than those applicable to other senior executives of the Company.

## 5.

BENEFITS AND EXPENSES

**5.1 Benefits.** The Employee may participate in all employee benefit plans that the Company maintains for its senior executives, subject to the terms of those plans.

**5.2 Vacation.** The Employee is entitled to 25 days of paid vacation per year, in addition to Company holidays.

**5.3 Expenses.** The Company shall reimburse the Employee for reasonable business expenses incurred in performing her duties, in accordance with Company policy.

**5.4 Patent Maintenance.** During the Term, the Company shall reimburse the Employee for the reasonable out-of-pocket costs of prosecuting and maintaining the Detector Calibration Patents.

## 6. TERMINATION OF EMPLOYMENT

**6.1 Death or Disability.** Employment terminates automatically on the Employee's death. The Company may terminate employment on 30 days' written notice if the Employee is unable, because of physical or mental incapacity, to perform her essential duties with or without reasonable accommodation for 120 consecutive days.

**6.2 By the Company.** The Company may terminate employment for Cause, or without Cause on 30 days' written notice.

**6.3 By the Employee.** The Employee may resign for Good Reason, or without Good Reason on 60 days' written notice.

**6.4 Accrued Obligations.** On any termination, the Company shall pay the Employee:

(a) earned but unpaid Base Salary;

(b) accrued but unused vacation;

(c) unreimbursed business expenses; and

(d) any vested benefits under Company plans.

These are the "**Accrued Obligations**."

## 7. SEVERANCE

**7.1 Qualifying Termination.** If the Company terminates the Employee's employment without Cause, or she resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay or provide the following, subject to Section 7.3:

(a) continued Base Salary for 12 months;

(b) a pro-rated target bonus for the year of termination; and

(c) Company-paid COBRA premiums for up to 12 months.

**7.2 Change of Control Termination.** If the qualifying termination described in Section 7.1 occurs within 12 months after a Change of Control, the following enhancements apply:

(a) the salary continuation period becomes 18 months;

(b) the Employee also receives a lump sum equal to 1.5 times her target bonus; and

(c) all unvested equity awards held by the Employee vest in full.

**7.3 Release.** Severance under this Section 7 is conditioned on the Employee executing, and not revoking, a general release of claims in favor of the Company in a form reasonably acceptable to the Company, within 60 days after termination.

**Re: Proposed Acquisition of Sorrelux Imaging, Inc.: Non-Binding Letter of Intent**

Ladies and Gentlemen:

This letter of intent (this "**Letter**") sets out the principal terms on which Daikesk Imaging Holdings, Inc. ("**Buyer**") proposes to acquire all of the issued and outstanding shares of capital stock (the "**Shares**") of Sorrelux Imaging, Inc. (the "**Company**") from Glosiv Medical Systems, Inc. ("**Seller**") (the "**Transaction**"). Except as provided in Section 13, this Letter is not binding. It is intended only as a basis for continued due diligence and for negotiation of definitive agreements.

## 1. Structure

Buyer will purchase all of the Shares from Seller under a stock purchase agreement (the "**Definitive Agreement**"). At closing (the "**Closing**"), the Company will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Buyer. Buyer will acquire the Company's operations as a going concern. Those operations comprise the design, manufacture, sale and servicing of digital radiography and ultrasound imaging systems (the "**Business**"), including the Company's field-service organization and installed-base service contracts.

## 2. Purchase Price

The aggregate purchase price for the Shares will be $186,500,000 (the "**Purchase Price**"), payable in cash at Closing. The Purchase Price assumes the following:

(a) the Company is delivered on a cash-free, debt-free basis; and

(b) the Company has a normalized level of working capital, to be agreed by the parties during due diligence.

The Purchase Price will be subject to a customary post-Closing working capital adjustment.

## 3. Escrow

At Closing, Buyer will deposit 5% of the Purchase Price ($9,325,000) with a mutually acceptable escrow agent. The escrow will serve as a source of recovery for indemnification claims under the Definitive Agreement.

## 4. Representations, Warranties and Indemnification

The Definitive Agreement will contain representations, warranties, covenants and indemnities customary for a transaction of this type. These will include representations about capitalization, title to the Shares, financial statements, material contracts, intellectual property, FDA regulatory compliance, data privacy and HIPAA, employees and taxes.

Buyer proposes the following indemnification terms:

(a) Seller's indemnification obligation for breaches of general representations and warranties will be capped at 10% of the Purchase Price;

(b) the cap in paragraph (a) will be subject to a deductible to be agreed; and

(c) fraud, fundamental representations and breaches of Seller's post-Closing confidentiality covenant will be excluded from the cap.

## 5. Transition Services

At Closing, Seller and the Company will enter into a transition services agreement (the "**Transition Services Agreement**"). Under it, Seller will provide the services that Seller or its Affiliates currently provide to the Company and that are reasonably necessary for the Company to continue to operate the Business as currently conducted. The term will be 12 months after the Closing Date. The services will include:

(a) information technology, ERP, network hosting, and data migration support;

(b) support for the Company's field-service operations, including dispatch, service-ticketing systems, spare-parts logistics and access to installed-base service records;

(c) support for the Company's ultrasound operations, including shared transducer sourcing, regulatory and complaint-handling systems, and distributor order processing;

(d) supply chain, procurement and shared-supplier arrangements for digital radiography detectors and components; and

(e) payroll, benefits administration, and finance and accounting support.

Services will be provided at Seller's fully loaded cost without markup, at a level of service consistent with that provided to the Company in the 12 months before Closing. The parties will set out a detailed services schedule in the Definitive Agreement process.

## 6. Key Personnel

Buyer places significant value on the Company's management and technical team. That team includes Dr. Tamsin Ferreol, the Company's Chief Technology Officer. During due diligence, Buyer expects to review the employment arrangements of senior Company personnel and any intellectual property licensed to the Company by those personnel. Buyer may also discuss retention arrangements with key personnel, with Seller's prior consent. Any such retention arrangements are to take effect at Closing.

(a) engage in the Business in North America or Europe; or

(b) solicit for employment senior employees of the Company, subject to customary exceptions.

## 8. Conditions

Closing will be subject to customary conditions, including:

(a) satisfactory completion of Buyer's business, financial, legal, regulatory and intellectual property due diligence;

(b) negotiation and execution of the Definitive Agreement and the Transition Services Agreement on terms satisfactory to Buyer and Seller;

(c) expiration or termination of any waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976;

(d) receipt of required third-party consents identified in due diligence;

(e) approval of the Transaction by Buyer's board of directors; and

(f) the absence of any material adverse change in the Company or the Business.

From the date of this Letter, Seller will cause the Company to give Buyer and its advisors reasonable access to the following during normal business hours:

(a) the Company's books, records, contracts, facilities and personnel; and

(b) the Company's regul

# MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

This MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of February 9, 2026 (the "**Effective Date**"), by and between **Daikesk Imaging Holdings, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Daikesk**"), and **Glosiv Medical Systems, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Glosiv**"). Daikesk and Glosiv are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Glosiv owns all of the issued and outstanding capital stock of Sorrelux Imaging, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "**Company**").

B. The Parties wish to evaluate and negotiate a possible negotiated transaction in which Daikesk would acquire the Company or its business (the "**Transaction**").

C. In connection with the Transaction, each Party expects to disclose to the other certain confidential and proprietary information, and the Parties wish to set out the terms on which that information will be protected.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Agreement, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 Defined Terms.** The following terms have the meanings set forth below:

"**Affiliate**" means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by or is under common control with that Person. For purposes of this Agreement, the Company is an Affiliate of Glosiv.

"**Confidential Information**" means all non-public information, in any form or medium, that a Disclosing Party or its Representatives furnish to a Receiving Party or its Representatives on or after the Effective Date in connection with the Transaction. It includes financial statements, forecasts, customer and supplier information, installed-base and field-service records, product designs, source code, regulatory submissions, intellectual property documentation, employee information and pricing. It also includes all notes, analyses, compilations and other materials prepared by the Receiving Party or its Representatives to the extent they contain or reflect that information, and the Transaction Information.

"**Disclosing Party**" means a Party, or its Affiliate, that discloses Confidential Information.

"**Person**" means any individual, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, trust, governmental authority or other entity.

"**Receiving Party**" means a Party that receives Confidential Information, whether directly or through its Representatives.

"**Representatives**" means, with respect to a Party, its Affiliates and its and their directors, officers, employees, agents, financing sources, and legal, financial, accounting and other professional advisors.

"**Transaction Information**" means the fact that Confidential Information has been made available, the fact that the Parties are discussing the Transaction, and the status and terms of those discussions.

**1.2 Interpretation.** Headings are for convenience only. "Including" means "including without limitation."

## 2. USE AND NON-DISCLOSURE

**2.1 Permitted Use.** The Receiving Party shall use Confidential Information solely to evaluate, negotiate and consummate the Transaction, and for no other purpose.

**2.2 Non-Disclosure.** The Receiving Party shall hold Confidential Information in strict confidence and shall not disclose it to any Person, except to its Representatives who:

(a) need to know the Confidential Information for the purpose described in Section 2.1;

(b) have been informed of its confidential nature; and

(c) are bound by duties or obligations of confidentiality at least as protective as those in this Agreement.

**2.3 Responsibility for Representatives.** Each Party is responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its Representatives, other than Representatives who have entered into a separate confidentiality agreement directly with the Disclosing Party.

**2.4 Standard of Care.** The Receiving Party shall protect Confidential Information using at least the degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, and in any event no less than reasonable care.

**2.5 Competitively Sensitive Information.** The Parties acknowledge that each of them participates in the medical imaging industry. A Disclosing Party may designate particular Confidential Information, such as customer-specific pricing, cost data or product road maps, as "Clean Team Only." The Receiving Party shall limit access to designated information to the individuals and outside advisors that the Parties approve in writing, and shall comply with any reasonable clean-team protocol the Parties agree in writing.

**2.6 Personal Health Information.** No Party shall disclose protected health information, as defined under HIPAA, to the other Party under this Agreement unless the information has first been de-identified in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.514.

## 3. EXCEPTIONS

**3.1 Excluded Information.** Confidential Information does not include information that the Receiving Party can demonstrate:

(a) is or becomes generally available to the public, other than through disclosure by the Receiving Party or its Representatives in breach of this Agreement;

(b) was lawfully in the Receiving Party's possession on a non-confidential basis before disclosure by the Disclosing Party;

(c) becomes available to the Receiving Party on a non-confidential basis from a source other than the Disclosing Party or its Representatives, if that source is not known by the Receiving Party to be bound by a confidentiality obligation to the Disclosing Party; or

(d) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to Confidential Information.

**3.2 Compelled Disclosure.** If the Receiving Party or any of its Representatives is required by law, regulation, stock exchange rule or legal process to disclose any Confidential Information, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permitted:

(a) give the Disclosing Party prompt written notice so th

If no protective order is obtained, the Receiving Party or its Representative may disclose only the portion of Confidential Information that its counsel advises is legally required, and shall use reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment of it.

## 4. CONTACTS; NON-SOLICITATION

**4.1 Contacts.** Without Glosiv's prior consent, Daikesk shall not, and shall direct its Representatives not to, initiate contact concerning the Transaction or the Confidential Information with any employee (other than those designated by Glosiv), customer, supplier, distributor or group purchasing organization of the Company. This Section 4.1 does not restrict contacts in the ordinary course of business unrelated to the Transaction.

**4.2 Non-Solicitation.** For 12 months after the Effective Date, Daikesk shall not, and shall cause its controlled Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly solicit for employment any officer or senior technical employee of the Company with whom Daikesk first had contact, or of whom Daikesk first became aware, in connection with the Transaction. This Section 4.2 does not prohibit (a) general solicitations, including through search firms, that are not targeted at Company employees, or hiring any person who responds to them, or (b) discussions with Company personnel to which Glosiv has given its prior consent.

## 5. RETURN AND DESTRUCTION

**5.1 Return or Destruction.** Within ten business days after the Disclosing Party's written request, or after either Party notifies the other that it has decided not to proceed with the Transaction, the Receiving Party shall return to the Disclosing Party, or destroy, all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party in its or its Representatives' possession. On request, an officer of the Receiving Party shall certify that destruction in writing.

**5.2 Retained Copies.** The Receiving Party and its Representatives may retain copies of Confidential Information to the extent required by law, regulation or bona fide internal document-retention policy, or stored in automatic electronic backup systems that are not readily accessible. Retained Confidential Information remains subject to this Agreement for so long as it is retained, notwithstanding expiration of the term under Section 8.1.

## 6. NO REPRESENTATIONS; NO LICENSE

**6.1 No Warranty.** Confidential Information is provided "as is." Neither Party nor its Representatives makes any representation or warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy or completeness of Confidential Information. Only the representations and warranties made in a definitive agreement for the Transaction, when executed and delivered, and subject to its terms, will have any legal effect.

**6.2 No License.** All Confidential Information remains the property of the Disclosing Party. Nothing in this Agreement grants the Receiving Party any license or other right in any patent, trademark, copyright, trade secret or other intellectual property of the Disclosing Party or its Affiliates.

## 7. NO OBLIGATION TO PROCEED

**7.1 No Commitment.** Neither Party is obligated to pursue or complete the Transaction unless and until a definitive agreement has been executed and delivered, and then only on the terms of that definitive agreement. Either Party may end discussions at any time for any reason by written notice to the other Party.

**7.2 Effect of Closing.** If the Transaction is consummated, Daikesk's obligations under this Agreement with respect to Confidential Information concerning the Company or its business terminate at the closing of the Transaction. All other obligations under this Agreement continue in accordance with their terms.

## 8. TERM

**8.1 Term.** This Agreement continues in effect for two years after the Effective Date. The Receiving Party's obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law continue for so long as that information remains a trade secret.

**8.2 Accrued Rights.** Expiration of this Agreement does not relieve any Party of liability for a breach occurring before expiration.

## 9. REMEDIES

**9.1 Equitable Relief.** Each Party acknowledges that a breach of this Agreement may cause the other Party irreparable harm for which money damages would not be an adequate remedy. The non-breaching Party is entitled to seek specific performance and injunctive relief, without proof of actual damages and without posting bond, in addition to any other remedy available at law or in equity.

**9.2 Costs.** If a court of competent jurisdiction determines in a final, non-appealable order that a Party or its Representatives breached this Agreement, that Party shall reimburse the other Party for its reasonable and documented legal fees and expenses incurred in connection with the litigation.

## 10. GENERAL

**10.1 Notices.** Notices must be in writing and are effective on delivery by hand, nationally recognized overnight courier or email (with confirmation of transmission), addressed:

If to Daikesk: Daikesk Imaging Holdings, Inc., Attention: General Counsel.

If to Glosiv: Glosiv Medical Systems, Inc., Attention: Chief Legal Officer.

**10.2 Amendment; Waiver.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No failure or delay in exercising any right under this Agreement operates as a waiver of it, and no waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving Party.

**10.3 Assignment.** Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party. Any purported assignment without that consent is void. This Agreement binds and benefits the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns.

**10.4 Securities Laws.** Each Party acknowledges that it is aware

**10.5 Privilege.** To the extent any Confidential Information includes materials subject to the attorney-client privilege, work product doctrine or other applicable privilege, the Parties share a common legal and commercial interest in those materials. Disclosure under this Agreement is not intended to waive any privilege or protection.

**10.6 Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force, and the invalid provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable.

**10.7 Governing Law.** This Agreement and all claims arising out of or relating to it are governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles that would require the application of the laws of another jurisdiction.

**10.8 Forum; Waiver of Jury Trial.** Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if that court lacks subject-matter jurisdiction, the Superior Court of the State of Delaware or the United States District Court for the District of Delaware) for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement. EACH PARTY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY SUCH ACTION.

**10.9 Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which constitute one instrument.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement as of the Effective Date.
